articles.title_zh: MGM China May Be Source of Allure If MGM Resorts Draws Another Suitor
articles.content_orig:
An amended voting agreement between MGM Resorts International (NYSE: MGM) and Barry Diller’s People Inc. (NASDAQ: PPLI) could make it easier for the casino operator to sell itself to another suitor in the future while potentially making MGM China a point of emphasis in a change of control scenario.
In a new report, CreditSights says MGM China faces some “event risk” if control of the Las Vegas-based parent changes hands. The research firm notes that “while the takeover overhang risk is less acute,” it’s also worth acknowledging that the altered voting agreement with Diller implies MGM is possibly open to selling itself in the future. The US-based parent owns 56% of the operator of MGM Cotai and MGM Macau. It’s possible that the Macau entity could be a source of attraction for a future MGM suitor.
“We would also not rule out MGM China’s continued strong operational performance (decent 3Q26 results with a stronger market share and leverage metrics remaining well below pre-pandemic levels) as a positive draw for potential buyers of MGM,” according to CreditSights.
MGM has made clear it’s not conducting talks in either direction regarding a transaction with Diller’s media consortium nor has the Bellagio operator stated that it’s in discussions with another prospective buyer.
One of the primary details in the new MGM/People agreement is that the media conglomerate, which controls approximately 26% of the gaming company’s shares, will pledge those shares “in accordance with the Board’s recommendation in connection with a change of control transaction.”
After disclosing an $18 billion takeover bid for the casino behemoth, Diller made clear he’d oppose third-party bids, but that stance changed by way of the fresh voting agreement. That shift could make it easier for MGM to sell itself in the future.
“ The amended voting agreement release between People Inc. and MGM, MGM’s Chairman noted it creates ‘a clear path to maximize value through share repurchases and a change of control (CoC) transaction, if applicable,’ which to us, reads as MGM leaving the door open to another potential acquirer, a possibility that could resurface especially if MGM’s stock price remains depressed,” adds CreditSights.
Where MGM China fits into a hypothetical change of control at MGM isn’t clear, but it’s not a stretch to assume most would-be buyers of the Cosmopolitan operator would want the Macau unit.
While a possible sale of the Las Vegas gaming giant may introduce event risk for the Macau entity, no transaction is on the table as of yet and if one comes to pass down the road, it could result in a favorable outcome or more clarity for MGM China.
Soon after Diller made his takeover overture for MGM, speculation surfaced — though it was never confirmed — that he wanted to unload the company’s MGM China stake as well as its interest in MGM Osaka.

articles.title_orig: Wear OS adding ‘system status bar’ to apps, Wear OS 7.1 coming
articles.title_zh: Wear OS adding ‘system status bar’ to apps, Wear OS 7.1 coming
articles.content_orig:
Earlier this week, Google revealed that a “later platform release of Wear OS” is adding a “system status bar.”
On October 26, Google released a Wear OS canary emulator in Android Studio to let developers “test upcoming platform features and user interface changes before they become available in a consumer platform release on physical devices.”
The upcoming feature in question is a “persistent system status bar over Wear OS app windows at the top position of the circular display.” It will display the “current time and system status indicators,” similar to Android on phones and tablets.
Additionally: “These indicators use standardized clock typography, placement, and backplate across the platform and different apps, including your app.” Apps that require a fullscreen experience will be able to hide the status bar.
As of this preview, “the system status bar displays a placeholder star icon instead of final system status indicators.”
This emulator is published as Wear OS 7.1 (API level 37.2-beta1, based on Android 17 “CinnamonBun”) with a CP41.260831.001.E8 build ID. This reveals that Wear OS 7.1 is coming, but it sounds like the status bar will launch in a later release: “The system status bar is included exclusively in this canary emulator to support early testing and feedback. It won’t be included in the upcoming Wear OS 7.1 stable emulator.”

articles.title_orig: Iran’s top diplomat hopes US shows ‘rationality,’ and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Iran’s top diplomat hopes US shows ‘rationality,’ and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
“Some progress” has been made in efforts to reach an agreement between the US and Iran, several sources familiar with the negotiations told The Jerusalem Post . However, the sources stressed that "significant gaps remain between the two sides".
“There is some optimism that an agreement can be reached. But there is still work to be done,” one source said.
Another source said no progress had been made on the nuclear issue and that the advances concerned other matters, including the timeline for implementing a potential agreement.
In recent days, Qatari mediators have intensified indirect diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran amid growing fears of a potential military escalation following the US midterm elections.
An Iranian delegation traveled to Doha for several days of talks, coordinated closely with Washington, following intensive consultations in Tehran. The discussions reportedly focus on proposals to de-escalate the eight-month-old conflict, including a potential two-day framework for reopening the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz and resuming broader peace negotiations.
Despite these diplomatic efforts, significant gaps remain between the two sides. Tehran is demanding that Washington lift recent sanctions, reinstate oil waivers, reduce its regional military presence, and end port blockades before addressing restrictions on Iran's nuclear program.
By contrast, US officials, following recent outreach by Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei , insist that any comprehensive agreement must address nuclear concerns from the outset.
On Sunday, US President Donald Trump was asked how negotiations with Iran were progressing.
“They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. They make a deal and then they back out,” he responded.
Trump also said there were “one or two sites” in Iran's nuclear program that the US needed to address.
“But we can do that in 10 minutes,” he added.
A source familiar with the matter confirmed to the Post that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Trump spoke by phone on Saturday. The call came days after Trump was briefed by US Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Adm. Brad Cooper on military options for a possible operation against Iran.
Meanwhile, Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad said Iran had no intention of negotiating over its nuclear program, regardless of the pressure exerted on it.
Dr. Raz Zimmt, head of the Iran and Shi'ite Axis Research Program at the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), told The Jerusalem Post that each side currently needs something from the other that cannot be reversed, while neither is willing to make what would constitute an irreversible concession.
“The Americans are prepared to lift the naval blockade and some of the sanctions, since these measures can be reinstated, and in return they are demanding something on the nuclear front, such as an inspectors' visit and/or action regarding the enriched uranium. The Iranians, meanwhile, are prepared to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and perhaps even allow inspectors to visit certain sites, but they are unwilling to give up their enriched uranium. Instead, they are demanding something permanent, such as the unfreezing of Iranian assets.
“I find it difficult to see how this deadlock can be resolved,” Zimmt said.
Nevertheless, he added that, given the risks of another round of military confrontation, he would not rule out the possibility that the two sides could ultimately reach a compromise, even if only a temporary one.

articles.title_orig: AI investors hedge against losses amid tech stock selloff
articles.title_zh: AI investors hedge against losses amid tech stock selloff
articles.content_orig:
Investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence's potential to transform the global economy has fueled massive bets on the sector; however, growing concerns about a possible downturn are prompting investors to seek financial protection against losses, The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday.
“We’re seeing really significant demand from folks looking to protect downside,” said Stephen Solaka, a senior vice president at Gateway Investment Advisers.
Investors and technology executives are increasingly turning to financial instruments such as put options and credit-default swaps to protect their investments.
Put options give investors the right to sell shares at a predetermined price before a specified date. For shareholders seeking protection, these contracts can limit potential losses if stock prices fall sharply, although investors must pay a premium for that protection.
A combination of rising borrowing costs for major data center projects and chip purchases, falling share prices among AI companies, and a broader stock market selloff has heightened concerns about the sector's financial outlook.
Friday's technology stock selloff wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value. The Nasdaq 100 index fell 3.4%, while the broader S&P 500 dropped 1.8%. The S&P 500's technology sector was hit particularly hard, declining more than 4.2%, NBC News reported Friday.
The growing demand for financial protection comes as AI companies continue seeking enormous amounts of capital to fund infrastructure development and expansion.
According to Solaka, some investors have accumulated such substantial gains from technology stocks that they now prioritize protecting their wealth over pursuing further returns.
“These people have made so much money, they’re quitting to hedge their stock,” Solaka said, adding that some companies restrict employees’ trades.
For example, trading in put options tied to AI cloud infrastructure company CoreWeave surged to record levels in October and remained elevated, according to data from Cboe Global Markets.
Investors are also turning to credit-default swaps, financial contracts that protect against a borrower failing to repay its debt.
According to the report, the cost of insuring against debt defaults by major technology companies, including Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle, rose over the past month to its highest level since 2021.
“There were no exceptions, suggesting broad market concern about the sector rather than idiosyncratic credit events at individual companies,” said Eugene Grinberg, a co-founder of bond data provider Solve.
As investment in AI infrastructure grows, trading firm Jump Trading has begun offering financial contracts that allow companies to protect themselves against a potential collapse in the price of computing power.
For example, companies renting out Nvidia chips could use these contracts to lock in a minimum rental price, protecting revenue if demand for AI computing power falls.
The growing demand for financial protection is reminiscent of the events depicted in The Big Short , when investors used credit-default swaps to bet against mortgage-backed securities before the 2008 financial crisis. Unlike those investors, however, many of today's technology shareholders are not necessarily betting on a market collapse, but seeking to protect gains accumulated during the AI boom.

articles.title_orig: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
articles.title_zh: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.
The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.
It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.
The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.
Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.
In an address to the nation to mark Antigua and Barbuda's independence day, Prime Minister Gaston Browne said the history of slavery was painful and "its consequences have not disappeared with the passage of time".
He said the country's pursuit of reparatory justice deserved "seriousness, sensitivity and sustained international engagement".
Browne went on to say his government was having these conversations in bilateral discussions with the UK and other Commonwealth countries at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.
She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."
The King will make his speech at the CHOGM.
He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.
"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."
When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".
The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.
On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".
In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.
Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.
Royal sources have stressed that the decisions around making an apology are a matter for government, not the Palace.
"His Majesty is well practised on the diplomatic tightrope," a Royal aide said. "He is up for challenging visits with complex issues and relationships in play. He sees it as his role to 'bat for Britain', the Realms and wider Commonwealth."
In a piece for the Guardian published on Friday night, Burnham described the transatlantic slave trade as a "brutal and barbaric violation" , and that Britain "must face up to the past".
His separate pledge in his article to strengthen the work of the Commonwealth as an organisation will be welcomed by King Charles, who views the collection of 56 countries as a powerful vehicle for change.
The King will be giving the opening speech at CHOGM, which gathers leaders from those 56 states every two years in a different part of the Commonwealth.
Each biennial meeting has a theme and this year's is officially called Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.
Queen Camilla is with the King in Antigua and, as the couple attended a church service on Sunday morning ahead of joining celebrations to mark Independence Day on the island, there was a reminder of what the intended focus of the week will be.
Bishop of North Eastern Caribbean and Aruba,  Ernest Flemming, told the congregation the "prosperity" of the Commonwealth must be a "shared prosperity".
"True partnership requires mutual respect, it requires listening, it requires fairness."
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson said: "Institutions are under strain across the globe. The Commonwealth has scale and breadth, but is also small enough for leaders to know each other and co-operate together."
The King, they said, "contributes ideas and encouragement on a wide range of issues, delivering practical results which help improve the lives of millions".
It has been a difficult few months for the King, with developments surrounding his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor , and the publication of a book by his former brother-in-law, Earl Spencer.
In addition, his son the Duke of Sussex made a surprise move back to the UK with his wife Meghan and their two children in August.
Asked if the King was confident that his approach to family matters had been the right one in terms of public attitudes towards the institution, the response was concise. "Yes," a senior aide told the BBC. "That is why he takes the actions he does - and has done."
On the serious allegations that have emerged about Meghan's father , Thomas Markle, the Palace did not want to get involved publicly: "We wouldn't comment on private family matters."
The King is also still being treated for cancer. He was diagnosed in early 2024 and the Palace says he remains on a "positive trajectory".
In hot and humid conditions, he will soon celebrate his 78th birthday and will have carried out about 36 engagements by the end of this nine-day tour of the Caribbean.

articles.title_orig: Creditor has "taken control" of forever cruise, message to residents shows
articles.title_zh: Creditor has "taken control" of forever cruise, message to residents shows
articles.content_orig:
Residents of Villa Vie Odyssey — which remains stuck in Cambodia —  have been informed the cruise ship is now under control of its lender, according to a message sent to residents and obtained by CBS News.
The ship will soon be moved from Cambodia to Singapore, where it could eventually be auctioned off, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. Company leadership, however, said they're optimistic they can get the ship back — if they find an operational partner.
"This is a 30- to 90-day process, and, during that process, we have time to get a restructure done," Mike Petterson, the company's founder and executive chairman, told CBS News.
Passengers had only the weekend to remove all of their belongings from the ship before it became inaccessible to them, as the lender took over the operational costs of the ship.
"They have now the responsibility to pay the crew, fuel and the operations of the vessel and safekeeping of the vessel," Petterson said, stressing that they're exploring options to keep the ship going. "They would be willing to work with a funded plan — they're not out of negotiations — it's not like you get your car repossessed and you can't get it back."
Some passengers expressed frustration with the company's optimistic tone and worried it gave some residents a sense of "false hope."
"The lender has taken possession of the ship, but that does not mean the Odyssey's future has been decided," the message to residents read, in part. "No sale has been scheduled. We believe there is time to bring forward a viable plan and are working to do that."
An effort by a group of residents to buy the ship from the company also failed, after a lender denied them funding, according to sources who spoke with CBS News. The effort had received pledges from 169 residents who were willing to put more money into the project.
Internal communications reviewed by CBS News showed the ship was in financial distress for at least three months prior to Cambodia. Now, additional documents show that the company had a sense of urgency in getting more residents to provide even more funds.
During a meeting that took place in early August, the company wrote in an internal PowerPoint presentation: "A significant new line of inquiry is the need to distinguish actual inability to contribute from unwillingness to contribute further."
Joel Greiff from Naples, Florida spent $350,000 on a cabin on board, but he spent just 26 days on the ship after moving into it in October. Greiff told CBS News he paid an initial deposit in August 2025 and paid the remainder in May 2026.
In late July, Greiff said he received a message from the company about its financial woes. At the time, the company was asking residents for more money to keep the ship afloat.
"I sell my RV on August 3rd and I'm like — oh," Grief said. "This is gonna fail. Every sign is there."
Since being kicked off the ship, he has found a place to live in Kompat, Cambodia.
"I went and found a place to stay for $200 a month. Beautiful place," he said. "It's right on the river. It's what I wanted and what I needed."
Greiff said he has come to terms with the fact that he may never see the money he invested in the ship again.
"I do not feel ill will, I just feel that they don't know how to run a business whatsoever," he said. "They might want to contemplate never running a business again."
It is still unclear what will happen to the Odyssey next, but, prior to becoming stranded in Cambodia, Residential Cruise Holdings, the parent company of Villa Vie, was in the process of acquiring at least one additional cruise ship and working on two residential cruise projects.
"I don't have any update on that," said Petterson. "Our focus is 100% on the Odyssey. Villa Vie was entirely capitalized by the residents themselves. There is no stakeholder outside of the residents."
A Chapter 11 bankruptcy for Villa Vie would cost the ship about $3 million for the first 60 days of the process, according to the message sent to residents.
"The plan we are pursuing is to support those operations through DIP financing and resident maintenance collections," the message read. "The debt and legal issues are serious, but they do not erase the value of the ship, the resident community or the opportunity to build a stronger operating model. A structured transition with new capital and experienced operators can address the challenges and create a path forward."
Petterson said the company is entirely owned by employees and residents, "so, when there is a financial need, residents are by definition the shareholders of the company and are naturally asked as shareholders to contribute."
This story published first on CBS News at 2:42 p.m. on Nov. 1, 2026.

articles.title_orig: Investors pull billions in funds from Binance after record $6.3bn hack
articles.title_zh: Investors pull billions in funds from Binance after record $6.3bn hack
articles.content_orig:
Cryptocurrency exchange has begun to allow withdrawals after theft believed to have come from North Korea
Investors have pulled $3.6bn (£2.7bn) in funds from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance as it recovers from a record hack in which billions were stolen from customer accounts.
The platform was hit by a $6.3bn theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history. Experts identified North Korea as the probable culprit .
Binance initially froze withdrawals as it investigated the breach but on Sunday announced it had begun a phased reopening .
By Sunday afternoon, the platform had processed $4.6bn in withdrawals and $1bn in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of about $3.6bn – representing 2.1% of its $171bn in total assets under management.
The numbers were confirmed by the company in its latest proof of reserves snapshot. A full report is expected on Monday.
Binance said: “After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising as expected, while deposit volumes have remained substantial.”
The crypto exchange told its customers that market conditions were stable and that its team was “testing rigorously the remaining networks and assets”.
“We know how important safe and reliable access to your funds is and will share details of the next phase as soon as we can,” it said on X.
In the first phase Binance restored withdrawals for 15 networks and assets, including ethereum, USDT and USDC tokens on the ethereum blockchain, as well as some others held on the BNB Smart Chain blockchain. Later on Sunday, dealing in the Dogecoin and Avalanche currencies resumed on their own platforms.
The platform said it had replenished 90% of the ⁠amount stolen. The remaining 10% of tokens were less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday.
Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and users would not bear the financial impact of the hack.
On Saturday the FBI confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.
“The Federal Bureau of Investigation is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29,” the law enforcement agency said.
after newsletter promotion
The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors” were “using to launder these stolen assets”.
Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside about $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.
The money spent rebuying tokens came from using part of its $1bn secure asset fund for users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its futures insurance fund and own corporate treasury, Binance said ​on X.
The hack came as many observers expressed worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.
The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

Houston and nine of its suburbs are earning new acclaim on U.S. News and World Report's just-released list of the best U.S. cities for retirees in 2027. Two northern suburbs, The Woodlands and Spring , are resting easy among the top five nationwide.
The 2027 Best Places to Retire list evaluated over 850 U.S. cities based on six livability metrics that best serve American retirees: quality of life, affordability, health care, retiree taxes, job market, and population and migration. The top 250 finalist cities were then ranked nationally and by city size.
Midland, Michigan topped the list for the second consecutive year and is followed by Homosassa Springs, Florida (No. 2) and Weirton, West Virginia (No. 3).
The Woodlands and Spring respectively maintained their standings as the No. 4 and No. 5 best cities for retirees for the second year in a row . The Woodlands topped the separate list of the best midsized U.S. cities to retire, while Spring landed 5th among the smallest U.S. cities.
Houston proper was declared the No. 2 best big city for retirees, and it ranked 89th overall. Elsewhere in the metro, Pearland (No. 13) and Conroe (No. 14) ranked just outside the overall top 10 but ranked 4th and 5th among the best midsized cities for retirees.
U.S. News said affordability is the "most considered factor" when it comes to picking the best place to live a low-stress retirement life, and that's what Houston and its neighbors deliver. Affordable cities also give retirees "a sense of security and comfort as they live out their golden years," according to Megan Wood, U.S. News assistant managing editor of home services and real estate.
"It’s no secret that affordability is top of mind for Americans this year, which is why U.S. News updated its weighting criteria to better align with what retirees prioritize," Wood said. "The 2027 rankings reflect key metrics used to highlight the places that best suit retiree needs."
Sugar Land was declared the 10th best place to live in the U.S. in a separate U.S. News report earlier this year, but it doesn't quite meet the expectations for retirees. This particular suburb ranked as the 45th best overall city to retire, but it fared better in the city size ranking and landed 13th among the biggest U.S. cities.
Pasadena also surprised as the 85th best place to retire nationwide in this report, despite being hailed as the No. 3 best city to retire in Texas by RetirementLiving.com.

articles.title_orig: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
articles.title_zh: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
articles.content_orig:
A rare species of beetle has been found in Pembrokeshire after not being seen in Wales for 60 years.
The Short-Necked Oil Beetle is named after the adult beetles' stubby shape and its ability to secrete an oily yellow-orange substance from its knee joints when alarmed.
They were not reported in the UK for almost 60 years after 1948 as habitat loss brought the species to the brink of extinction.
Anne Hobbs, from the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, said it was "very exciting" that the evidence suggested the species was breeding in Wales again.
The Short-Necked Oil Beetle is classed as nationally rare within Great Britain and listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List .
It is dependent on solitary bees for its lifecycle and needs a particular habitat to survive, with thick vegetation for shelter and dense flower coverage both essential.
The larvae of Short-Necked Oil Beetles lurk among flowers, waiting for a passing bee to carry them back to its nest, where they feed on the pollen the bee has collected.
Last year, the survey at Castlemartin found only dead adults of this particular beetle, raising concerns about the future of this species and its continued presence on the site.
But this year, after three years of searching, experts discovered larvae of the beetle on a small area of the site, suggesting that surveyors had managed to find some of the hatchlings from a larger batch of immature beetles.
The number and distribution of the beetle larvae seen also supported this, according to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).
They can typically be found from March to June in flower-rich coastal grassland and sand dune habitat, and are most active on warm, sunny days.
Adults can grow up to 24mm (0.9in) in length and the life span of an adult is approximately one year.
NRW said these conditions mean there are only a handful of suitable sites in the UK.
They were rediscovered in Devon in 2006 and on the Isle of Coll, in Scotland, in 2009. Since then, populations have been found on Tiree, Islay, Barra and Uist.
Castlemartin Range, in Pembrokeshire, is currently the only place in Wales where the species can be found and it is being consistently surveyed by conservationists.
The project is part of Wales's "flagship species recovery programme", said NRW, which works to conserve the Short-Necked Oil Beetle Sand other species that share similar habitats.
Hobbs described the Short-Necked Oil Beetle as an "amazing creature" and said their work needed to consider the "needs of several species to be effective".
She thanked their partners and volunteers for their continued support, despite having two years without a larval sighting.
"We look forward to the continued management of the site so that this amazing species can survive now and into the future."

Regional leaders called for calm Saturday as fears of a new escalation between the U.S., Israel and Iran grow.
Speaking at a security forum in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs said the message from the region is that it wants a return to peace. Also at the forum, Syria’s foreign minister said his country and Jordan would discuss ways to strengthen their shared border.
Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Saturday. Read our full coverage here.
On Saturday, Saudi Arabia’s vice minister of foreign affairs said the message from the region is that it wants a return to peace. Speaking at a security forum in Bahrain, Waleed ElKhereiji told the audience that efforts were being made to prevent a military escalation and reach an agreement that ends the crisis with Iran.
“If you look at … the efforts that everybody is trying to do, the message is very clear. People in this part of the world want to bring peace back to the region," he said. But he said no one can predict the outcome of the efforts.
Concerns are rising about a return to an all-out Iran war.
Speaking at the same event, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said an escalation in the region would be extremely destructive.
“We are very confident that … the second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere,” he said.
Syria’s Foreign Minister said Saturday that border security is a shared responsibility between his country and Jordan and that a high-level meeting is expected next month to discuss arrangements.
Speaking Saturday at the security forum in Bahrain, Assad al-Shibani said there are no “skirmishes” between the countries.
The announcement came after Jordanian strikes in Syria raised tensions between the neighbors.
Jordan said the strikes over Syria last week killed 20 militants from the extremist Islamic State group, but acknowledged that civilians had also been killed in the attacks. Syrian authorities reported seven people killed in the strikes, most of them women and children.
Separately, al-Shibani said Syria is in discussions to evaluate joining the Mecca Pact, the Saudi-led defense alliance that includes Turkey and Pakistan.
“Whether Syria joins or not, Syria thinks the region is in dire need of a structure that protects its security,” he said.

Sunday Preview – The Khazalite Holds prepare to march out
The duardin of the Khazalite Holds have remained hidden long enough. Next week, they begin the march out to bring their vengeance to the Mortal Realms with a range of new miniatures, rules, and more.
High Kyng Valankrom was crowned by Grungni himself to lead the duardin into a prosperous new era. Armed with the mighty hammer Bharadreng, he smashes his way through enemy lines atop his War Throne. This stunning centrepiece miniature can alternatively be built as a regular Thrynn on War Throne.*
A Thrynn is a lord of the karaks. Well-armed and armoured, they lead the war throng into battle, inspiring the brave duardin of the clans to settle their grudges .*
Runewrights are the magic users of the Khazalite Holds, harnessing the power that rises deep within the earth and containing it inside runes. With precise blows from their forgehammers, they can enhance the potency of these runes.*
Valayan Guardians are among the finest and bravest warriors of the karak. They can be armed with either runic halberd or rune axes and shields, and the kit includes parts to build an optional champion. In battle, they can make extensive use of the We Honour Valaya Ancestral Vow to make them even more resilient.*
Equipped with robust firearms, Clangunners unleash deadly salvos that pierce armour and gouge flesh. They can be armed with the longer-ranged Thrundok rifle or the unsubtle Thrundrin shotcannon. The kit also includes parts to build an optional champion, standard bearer, and drummer (who can choose between two different drums), and each of the regular Clangunners has a choice of two heads, making it easy to customise your unit.*
Ormyr is a nomadic Fyreslayer who often appears on the eve of battle to lend his strength-at-arms to the duardin cause. He’s accompanied by Ashtongue, a Kyndledroth that he rescued from the clutches of hobgrots. Together, they bring the fiery vengeance of the Grimmdron down upon their foes.*
Hjulda Drakkblud is the last of her clan. She ventures forth to reclaim fallen karaks, hopeful that the next one she liberates will be her former home. In battle, she swings her mighty two-handed axe Azangrom, cutting down any foolish enough to get in the way of her quest.*
Clanshields are the tough and reliable core infantry of the Khazalite Holds. They are ideal for holding key objectives, and will fight to avenge their fallen kin. This incredibly versatile kit is packed with options, making it simple to customise your doughty warriors.*
Rain down fire on your enemies from afar with the devastating Oathkeeper Cannon. It excels at killing enemy monsters, or similarly large and tough targets. The kit can alternatively be built as a Stonebreaker Mortar, a war machine for wiping out hordes of infantry.*
Gholems are revered living statues that make for imposing figures on the battlefield. Crafted into simulacra of the Keeper of the Gate himself, the Gholems of Gazul are armed with massive two-handed hammers to smash through enemy lines. The kit can alternatively build Gholems of Valaya, armed with huge axes and massive shields, making them archetypal defenders of the hearth.*
The miniatures in the Khazalite Holds Army Set made a complete Spearhead, and now the duardin are getting a second one, themed around the Fyreslayers.* This packed box set includes:
– 1 Auric Runefather on Magmadroth – 1 Auric Runesmiter – 9 Vulkyn Flameseekers – 5 Auric Hearthguard
Add a force of angry, vengeance-seeking Fyreslayers to any Grand Alliance: Order army. These Grimmdron hit hard and open up new tactical options for a range of different forces.* This kit includes:
– 1 Grimhold Exile – 1 Auric Flamekeeper – 5 Hearthguard Berzerkers
The Khazalite Holds battletome is filled with background and lore about these mountain-dwelling duardin, inspiring artwork and painted miniatures, and the rules you need to use them in your games of Warhammer Age of Sigmar. It’s the ideal guide for the game’s newest faction.
Battletome: Khazalite Holds will also be available in a Gamer’s Edition version. This smaller-format book includes the same content as the standard version, and also comes with 53 reference cards. The Gamer’s Edition is only available while stocks last.*
Honour the Ancestor Gods with a set of Khazalite Holds dice. Cast in frosted green acrylic plastic with gold in markings, they feature the faction logo on the ‘6’ face, and are only available while stocks last.*
The Khazalite Holds also feature in November’s issue of White Dwarf, with interviews with the miniatures designers of the new range, the ’Eavy Metal team, and the artists behind the artwork in the battletome. The Adeptus Custodes star in a battle report, and there’s all your usual White Dwarf favourites.
In the wake of the Horus Heresy, the Loyalists continue their crusade for vengeance by heading to Mars to reclaim the red planet. Wrath of Terra by John French follows the fighting against the Dark Mechanicum, the political posturing on Terra, and the Blood Angels as they try to come to terms with the death of Sanguinius.
Wrath of Terra will be available in a standard hardback edition and a premium edition, featuring a black leather-effect cover with silver-finish medallion on the front. This will be your first chance to buy this edition, which is only available while stocks last, but may return to print at a later date.

articles.title_zh: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries

Kremlin says Kyiv is ‘simply ignoring’ US wishes days before midterm elections after reported strikes on two oil sites
Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections, as a ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky ended on Sunday night.
Russian state media said on Sunday Ukrainian long-range drones had set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, soon after a major strike against another big refinery in Samara oblast, owned by the Russian state energy giant Rosneft.
The Wall Street Journal had reported that Ukraine had given in to pressure from the White House to stop bombing Russian energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian officials, however, told the Kyiv Independent newspaper that they never agreed to a demand from Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law, to pause refinery strikes for 30 days. The raids on Russia restarted on Friday, Kremlin officials said, complaining that Kyiv was now “simply ignoring” US wishes.
Trump has blamed the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , for the rise in global fuel prices, and last month lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel.
Zelenskyy has not acknowledged the latest refinery attacks, in an apparent attempt to avoid angry US reprisals. Instead, he said his armed forces had hit a defence industry enterprise in Russia’s Rostov region that made missiles. A Pantsir missile system was destroyed, he said, as part of Ukraine’s continuing “long-range sanctions”.
Zelenskyy said his country was obliged to retaliate because of a remorseless campaign by Moscow, using drones and ballistic missiles, against vulnerable city-based energy facilities. Four Ukrainian regions were hit by Russia overnight, with electricity cut as a result in hundreds of thousands of households.
“The intensity of the strikes is very high, and the Russians are seeking to maximally exploit the ​deficit of ballistic missile interceptors,” the Ukrainian president said on Telegram. Kyiv experienced power cuts lasting eight to 10 hours on Sunday after a critical thermal power plant was damaged.
Zelenskyy said Russia was suffering record losses, with 54,400 military personnel killed and wounded in October – the highest monthly figure since the full-scale war began. He said Ukraine recaptured 96.2 sqkm (37 sq miles) of its territory last month, 10.4 sqkm (4 sq miles) more than Moscow managed to seize, and emphasised: “Russia is losing.”
The latest attacks came before a six-day local ceasefire brokered by the US first lady, Melania Trump, came to an end in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. Hundreds of residents were reunited with their loved ones over the weekend in northern Ukraine, with both sides hailing the evacuation mission as a success.
“The ceasefire, which was in effect from October 27 to November 1, has ended,” said Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, hailing what had been an “important step in our joint humanitarian efforts”.
after newsletter promotion
Ukrainian observers say the Russian military used the truce to reinforce its positions and to swap hungry and exhausted troops garrisoned in Oleshky. The town sits on the left bank of the Dnipro River, to the east, and is opposite the larger city of Kherson, which Ukraine recaptured in autumn 2022. A renewed Russian onslaught is inevitable, the observers believe.
The pope said on Sunday he hoped cooperation between ⁠Russia and Ukraine in implementing the Oleshky ceasefire – the most significant since 2022 – would ⁠pave the ⁠way ​for broader peace efforts.
“I hope that the cooperation between the parties, which made this necessary humanitarian gesture possible, will strengthen their willingness to engage in dialogue,” he said during his Sunday prayer.
Trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US are likely to take place later this month, and Kremlin officials said on Sunday that Vladimir Putin was willing to talk directly to Zelenskyy by phone. They added that European leaders who support Ukraine should not be involved in any such call.
There is little prospect of a wider breakthrough, however, as the Russian president’s maximalist demands remain unchanged. He is insisting that Ukraine give up all of the eastern Donetsk oblast – which Russia has been unable to seize since 2014 – as well as further territory in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia provinces, which the Kremlin does not control but says it has “annexed”.

articles.title_orig: Exit polls suggest that Yotova wins runoff to become Bulgaria’s first elected female president
articles.title_zh: Exit polls suggest that Yotova wins runoff to become Bulgaria’s first elected female president
articles.content_orig:
Published: 15:51 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EDT, 1 November 2026
Exit polls in Bulgaria suggest acting President Iliana Yotova is set to become the country's first elected female head of state.
Ms Yotova, 62, secured around 52 per cent of the vote in Sunday's presidential run-off and was endorsed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev's Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party.
Her rival, pro-Western candidate Andrey Gyurov, received around 44 per cent.
The final official result is expected on Monday as the ballots are counted.
The vote was the first major test for Prime Minister Rumen Radev's Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party.
In April's parliamentary vote, the party won 131 of the 240 seats in Parliament, securing an outright majority.
Observers say that a victory for Ms Yotova will keep the presidency in the hands of the governing majority.
Such a concentration of power could prevent the effective maintenance of checks and balances on policy decisions by institutions, they say.
The exit polls put voter participation at about 27 per cent to 29 per cent, a bit higher than the first-round race on October 25, which had a record-low turnout of 23 per cent.
Incumbent President and presidential candidate Iliana Yotova casts her vote in Sofia, Bulgaria
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev speaks after the first exit polls of the second round of the presidential election, flanked by Presidential candidate and incumbent President Iliana Yotova
Ms Yotova took over the presidency in January, when Mr Radev stepped down to run for parliament, and was seeking her own elected mandate.
She's expected to continue Mr Radev's policy of keeping Bulgaria on its European path, while also supporting better relations with Russia and the lifting of sanctions.
The election comes amid growing tensions linked to Russia's war in Ukraine, following a series of drone attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea, which have raised security concerns in the region.
About two dozen seafarers are feared dead, and the strikes have prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security.
On Wednesday, a Greek container ship sank after being hit by sea drones.
Both candidates have called for a diplomatic end to the conflict, although they differ in their approach to relations with Russia and Ukraine.
Ms Yotova has proposed a security meeting involving all six Black Sea countries to seek a moratorium on hostilities, while Bulgaria has faced criticism over its cautious response to the maritime drone attacks.
She became acting president in January after Mr Radev resigned to enter and win a parliamentary race on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket.
People gather to stage a protest against President Iliana Yotova and Prime Minister Rumen Radev in front of the presidential palace in Sofia, Bulgaria
After casting her vote on Sunday, Ms Yotova said that she voted for a Bulgaria that makes its own decisions and maintains a strong voice on the international stage.
Ms Yotova said on Sunday: 'I voted for Bulgaria to be a strong state in a strong Europe, but for Bulgaria to have its own foreign policy and a voice when it needs to stand up for what matters most — the national interest.'
Mr Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine.
He said after voting: 'Today I voted for a secure, stable and European Bulgaria.'
The Balkan country joined Nato in 2004 and the European Union in 2007.
While there is a broad consensus among the parties in parliament on the country's pro-Western path, widespread pro-Russia sentiments based on traditional historical and cultural ties with Russia have divided society, particularly since the start of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, triggering the largest conflict in Europe since the Second World War.
The war has drawn in billions of pounds in Western military and financial support for Kyiv, while prompting sweeping sanctions against Moscow and raising security concerns across eastern Europe.

Everyone is frothing at the mouth over Gears of War E:Day again, but this time it’s not the culture war.
It's the sensationalized reporting around it's budget and retail sales. Headlines claim the game cost an astronomical $500 million to make, while other reports suggest it " only" sold 400,000 retail copies. Predictably, the terminally online commentary machine is in full force, with some rather insanely blaming Xbox fans for this failure.
Xbox fans asked for exclusives, and yet when push comes to shove, "fans didn't put their money where their mouth was," making Gears of War: E-Day's reported failure "their fault." It’s a neat and tidy narrative for console warriors, but one that’s completely out of touch with modern gaming economics outside of the social media bubble. First of all, that $500 million figure requires crucial context before anyone uses it as a stick to beat the game with.
As clarified by Derek Reese, former Senior Product Manager of Xbox Game Creator Services , that cost isn't simply the game's direct production budget. Much of that figure stems from broad operational overhead, with The Coalition essentially being on the hook for funding Microsoft's custom internal branch of Unreal Engine and supporting engine integration across the wider Xbox studio network (a tech-debt burden similar to Turn 10 bearing the operational costs for ForzaTech, on Fable and Forza Horizon ). Conflating general engine-R&D operational overhead with the direct cost of a single game's development represents a misleading omission in the wider narrative. Beyond the budget discourse, expecting Xbox players to subscribe to Game Pass Ultimate at $22.99 a month, and an annual commitment of over $275, AND drop $70 on day one for every first-party title just to prop up traditional sales metrics is both unrealistic and absurd. The suggestion that players need to pay twice to prove they support a studio fundamentally misunderstands why Microsoft built this system in the first place.
For what many are spending on an Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscription , in standard retail that represents the cost of roughly four full priced $70 AAA games. When a player opts into the Game Pass ecosystem, they are effectively pre-paying for their gaming line-up up front. Expecting that same consumer to buy Gears of War E: Day at retail price to satisfy outdated quarterly sales charts ignores the basic economic contract of a subscription service. The entire value proposition of Game Pass is that you don’t have to shell out $70 every time a major title lands. Not only that, but framing Game Pass users as passive freeloaders ignores key data we already know. Under oath, during the FTC proceedings, Xbox President at the time Sarah Bond revealed that Game Pass subscribers actually spend 20% more money on average on gaming than those who don’t subscribe. I too have pleaded with fans to “put their money where their mouth is” for Microsoft's divested teams like Undead Labs. There's a clear distinction between asking players to support a core Microsoft internal studio, whose quarterly profits are in the tens of billions, over supporting the newly independent Undead Labs. Players who are financially able , could buy State of Decay 3 to stick it to Microsoft's bean counters, and show Xbox what they had just given up.
The Coalition is a victim of Microsoft's structuring. Putting them on the hook for Unreal Engine support across multiple games, collaboration with Epic Games, while also building a multi-faceted multiplayer title squashed under Call of Duty : MW4, World of Warcraft : Forever, Grand Theft Auto 6, and various other heavy hitters this quarter is pure insanity.
In a single two-month span, gamers were asked to choose between massive titles across every sub-genre: Marvel’s Wolverine , Silent Hill: Townfall, Minecraft Dungeons 2 , Ace Combat 8 and major remasters like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Dynasty Warriors 3 Complete Edition.
Expecting any single game to generate record-breaking direct $70 sales during one of the most crowded, wallet-draining launch windows in recent gaming history is wishful thinking. In a climate where players are already triaging their spending, a day-one Game Pass entry was an incredibly convenient and lower-cost way to play E-Day.
Regardless, simply citing 400,000 unit sales, or focusing on Steam copies, vastly misrepresents the actual paying audience. Game Pass subscribers actually engaged with the game's revenue model in a massive way through the $30 Premium Edition Upgrade . That’s much easier to justify purchase-wise when you feel like you're already getting something of value with your subscription. How many would have spent ANYTHING on the game without it being on Game Pass? How do we really predict that behaviour? There's no "alternative reality generator" to see how the game would've shored up in a universe without Game Pass, GTA 6, or the rest of it.
The $70 premium SKU is, for all practical purposes, functionally dead for first-party titles on Xbox console. But that isn’t because Xbox players refuse to spend money; it's because Microsoft has trained them to spend money on early-access add-ons rather than $70 on a standalone license.
The same people attacking Xbox Game Pass are likely the same kind of people happy to wait for Steam sales, which too have contributed to a rejection of the $70 retail model. This is before we even talk about free-to-play titles like Fortnite, Roblox, mobile games, and others which actually dominate the spend.
For many of these people, it represents a glaring double standard to mock players for using the exact monetization model Xbox has designed for them.
The second major flaw in the current discourse is the demand for seemingly instant gratification. Asha Sharma positioned Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution as console exclusives at this years Xbox Games Showcase as something of an olive branch to the community. A signal that platform exclusivity was still a core priority for Xbox. But one game was never going to turn around hardware sales overnight. The reality of today’s market comes down to demographics and household finances.
Just a short story from my own experience showing a colleague E-Day running on a Xbox ROG Ally X during a train ride for work. He was blown away by the visuals and fondly recalled buying an Xbox console specifically for the original Gears of War. But today, as he told me, he has a PS5 , a mortgage, and a family. Knowing E-Day isn't on PlayStation was a bummer for him as he was genuinely interested in the game, but dropping significant cash on a secondary console for a single game simply isn't a justifiable household expense anymore for him.
Decisions like that aren't made on impulse anymore for the age and demographic of console users Xbox is targeting. Hardware momentum won’t be rebuilt with a single flagship release; it needs to be a slow and steady rebuild over years of consistent, uninterrupted hits. As a family, we have discussed buying a Nintendo Switch 2, driven in part by Ocarina of Time’s launch, but that alone isn’t a driving factor; we’ll get access to Pokopia, Mario Kart, Donkey Kong Bonanza, etc. – al

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Patents an AI That Can Literally Put Words in People’s Mouths in Real Time
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Patents an AI That Can Literally Put Words in People’s Mouths in Real Time
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft just filed a patent for an AI product that would be able to transform live video in real time to alter speakers’ words and faces.
The patent, as first flagged by patent-tracker Patentlyze , is described by its inventors as a “near real-time artificial intelligence (AI) enhancement of video or augmented reality (AR) presentations of live events.”
Using AI agents, the system would identify and alter or remove certain words, while editing a speaker’s face and mouth to match. The agents would rely on set parameters or user profiles to make the changes, and would also edit the video and audio just before and after a removed or replaced word to allow for “smooth transitions.”
In an era of media and the internet increasingly defined by AI-fueled deepfakes, disinformation, and information-muddling slop, the system described in this patent may represent a new world of filtering tools that subtly alter reality as it takes place, in this case on a highly-personalized level. Viewers, the patent suggests, could consume whatever live event they want to without hearing what they don’t want to hear.
The potential use cases floated in the patent vary. One possible application is real-time translation, with the system allowing for broadcasts and other live footage to be both heard and seen in a viewer’s preferred language.
The patent also posits that such a tool could be used to remove filler words like “um” or “ah” from live speech, or to erase stutters or speech impediments.
Other possible use cases, though, go much further. According to the patent, the system could be used to cut down on “personal words or phrases” like “coined terms,” as well as “colloquial terms” like the term “y’all” or the phrase “bite the bullet.” The patent also claims that the system could eliminate “mumbled words, mispronounced words, misused words, misspoken words, offensive words, insensitive words, or inappropriate words.” Replacement words, it adds, may come from an “internet search.”
In other words, live broadcasts may not be so live anymore after all.
Microsoft didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Dubbing has existed for ages, and video footage is edited all the time, both for normal and for insidious reasons. Automatically editing live videos in this way with the help of AI agents, however, could change how audiences fundamentally engage with live footage. As it stands, if people don’t like what they hear, they can simply turn something off; the system outlined by Microsoft describes an environment where people can instead adjust someone else’s speech to their personal taste. Language translation aside, does using a tool that eliminates errors, or erases words and phrases associated with a speaker’s local dialect, move us further into personalized bubbles? What’s so bad about hearing someone from the South say “y’all?”
To that end, the patent does mention that an event’s original live video and audio may be recorded and stored for the sake of “ground truth,” nodding to potential misuse and confusion that could arise from such a tool.
The kinds of live footage that could be transformed by the system include lectures, presentations, a range of television productions — awards ceremonies, game and cooking shows — and live sports, among several others.

articles.title_orig: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.title_zh: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.content_orig:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire.
In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy.
In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties.
The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information.
Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel.
"My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?"
At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre".
A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.
Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed.
Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled.
The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war.
The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.
Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title_orig: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.title_zh: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.content_orig:
Par Wan Xiubin, Zheng Hai'ou, Shao Yuzi, People's Daily
Above ground, expansive green spaces blend seamlessly with modern architecture. Beneath the surface, a network spanning more than 100 kilometers links underground utility corridors that deliver water, electricity, gas, heating, and communications.
In the cloud, a digital city is taking shape alongside the physical one, while the Xiong'an Urban Computing Center keeps watch over the entire city. A "city of the future" is steadily taking shape in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei province.
Rejecting sprawling, haphazard urban expansion, Xiong'an has adopted a different approach, with planning preceding construction, underground infrastructure built before above-ground development, and trees planted before the city takes shape. Modern governance has been integrated into every stage of urban development.
In the Rongdong area, the first developed urban area in Xiong'an, trees flourish and buildings stand in neat rows. There are no tangled overhead power lines, and the roads show no signs of repeated digging and patching.
This stability stems from an extensive underground utility tunnel system connecting parking facilities beneath 95 housing complexes. Using a hybrid of China's BeiDou satellite navigation and 5G indoor positioning, the system maintains reliable signals underground. Smart sensors distributed throughout the tunnels monitor environmental conditions in real time, enabling proactive maintenance. "Traffic flows smoothly both above and below ground. Living here feels safe and convenient," said Zhou Qiang, a local resident.
By prioritizing subsurface infrastructure, Xiong'an has built resilience into its foundation while deploying digital twin technology to create a synchronized virtual environment. Ma Yongjun, head of operations of the infrastructure construction company of China Xiong'an Group, starts each workday by logging into the digital twin system. The system provides a detailed view of the utility tunnels, with real-time updates on temperature, humidity, water pressure, and gas concentrations.
"When a problem arises, the system automatically issues an alert. It can be detected in the cloud and addressed directly inside the utility tunnel," Ma said.
Under clear autumn skies, birds flock to the Yannan dike of Baiyangdian Lake, while the Nanhe water conservancy hub is reflected in the water. The hub links the vast wetlands of Baiyangdian on one side with Xiong'an's modern buildings on the other.
Before the Xiong'an New Area was established, water quality across Baiyangdian was generally below Grade V, the lowest classification in the country's five-tier water quality system. Water flows had declined, and the waterways had become severely fragmented. At the Fuhe River estuary wetland, the gateway to Baiyangdian, polluted upstream water once flowed directly into the lake.
Zhu Baofeng, head of the water conservancy and water environment construction and operations division at China Xiong'an Group Ecological Construction Investment Co., Ltd., led his team in restoring the wetland through nature-based purification techniques, breathing new life into the wetland.
In recent years, Xiong'an has taken an integrated approach to replenishing water supplies, tackling pollution and preventing floods. It has advanced five major initiatives in parallel, including dredging waterways, linking lakes and ponds, restoring wetlands, replenishing water supplies in a science-based manner, and strengthening flood control.
"Baiyangdian has returned to its former vitality!" said Zhang Xuenong, chairman of the Baiyangdian Photographers Association in Anxin county, who has documented the lake's transformation in more than 100,000 photos. In recent years, rare birds such as the Baer's Pochard have frequently appeared in his photographs.
"The city and the lake now complement each other, and every shot captures a beautiful scene," Zhang said.
Water quality in Baiyangdian has remained stable at Grade III for five consecutive years. As of 2026, the number of wild bird species recorded there has risen to 296, up 90 from before the Xiong'an New Area was established. The number of fish species has recovered to 50.
"It feels like living in a garden," said Yuan Yuxin, a resettled resident who moved with his family into Lixian Garden residential community in Rongdong area in 2023.
"There's a supermarket just a few minutes' walk away, and my grandchildren live close to their schools. I play ball at the community senior care center every day. Life is fulfilling and comfortable," Yuan said.
In Nanwenying Community, where Yuan lives, household files document residents' needs and everyday concerns.
"We maintain individual files for each of our more than 3,700 households, covering matters such as health care and elderly care. We update them every two months," said Wang Weixiao, head of the Nanwenying Community.
The records have been organized into more than 80,000 entries and distilled into three lists covering available resources, residents' needs and concerns, and responsibilities. This helps streamline the many tasks involved in community governance, said Wang.
A settled home is the foundation for a fulfilling life. With equitable, high-quality public services, meticulous community-level governance and a thriving industrial base, Xiong'an is helping residents build settled homes and fulfilling lives.
"Governance is not something to be addressed after construction is complete. Xiong'an has integrated planning, construction and governance from the outset, ensuring that urban management is guided by clear rules from the very beginning," said Liu Zhenming, deputy director of the Natural Resources and Planning Bureau of the Xiong'an New Area.

The Trump State Department denounced the recent eastern Mediterranean maritime agreement between NATO member Turkey and the fractured Libyan state.
The Turkey-Libya deal has also caused frustration and anger among many nations because they say it rewrote the established sea borders of the sensitive Mediterranean Sea region, where large deposits of gas might be located.
The Eastern Libyan parliament approved the maritime accord in mid-October. The region is ruled by military leader Khalifa Haftar, who has formed an alliance with Turkey — the maritime deal ignores Libya’s internationally recognized government in Tripoli in the northwestern part of the oil-rich country.
A U.S. State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital: "The announcement of the ratification of the Turkish-Libyan delimitation memorandum of understanding has raised tensions in the region and is unhelpful and provocative — and our position on this matter has not changed."

The spokesperson added: "We encourage all countries, including partners in the Eastern Mediterranean, to resolve maritime disputes through good-faith negotiations and avoid any provocative behavior. Greece and Türkiye are both NATO allies . We encourage them to engage bilaterally to address any areas of disagreement."
According to the spokesperson, "Peaceful resolution of such disputes opens the way for commercial investment and exploration that will benefit the entire region."
According to the Turkish news agency Anadolu Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Wednesday said the maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya was "entirely legitimate" and not in violation of international law.
He added: "This is an entirely legitimate agreement, both from a legal and a political perspective. There is no need to debate it."
Reuters reported Fidan also shot back at critics of the deal. "There are countries reacting to this. We know why they are reacting. Some are doing so because they need to, some really do have strategic problems with this issue. ​ However, this is an entirely legitimate deal, both from a legal and a statutory perspective. ​There is no need to argue this."

Libya's military strongman Khalifa Haftar, center, attends a conference for the country's development and reconstruction on Sept 2024. (Khaled Nasraoui/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Images)

Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis angrily wrote on his ministry’s website that, "The memorandum will not be implemented. And it will not be implemented for the simple reason that it produces no legal effects whatsoever, as it is entirely contrary to international law." He added, "Türkiye had established a system of influence in Libya, essentially seeking to advance its own interests" and the Turkish media has ramped up its anti-Greece rhetoric. "There is a constant stream of reports pushing the Turkish government to become even more aggressive."
Endy Zemenides, the executive director of the Hellenic American Leadership Council, told Fox News Digital that the Turkey-Libya agreement "absolutely" endangers the security of the U.S. and its allies.
He said: "This memorandum specifically infringes on U.S. companies and U.S. energy policy. It effectively denies maritime rights and zones of Crete. Crete is NATO’s southernmost base. The European Union invoked unusually strong language targeting the deal, declaring it in violation of maritime law.
"The EU position regarding the MoU is firm and clear. As outlined in the European Council Conclusions of December 2019 and reiterated in June 2025, the Türkiye-Libya Memorandum of Understanding infringes upon the sovereign rights of third States and does not comply with the Law of the Sea. articles.title_orig: Israel’s president says parties need to engage with ‘open heart’ to avoid fresh election
articles.title_zh: Israel’s president says parties need to engage with ‘open heart’ to avoid fresh election
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his coalition’s parliamentary majority following legislative elections on October 27.
But a bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu also failed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.
What’s ahead is likely weeks of political wrangling as Israel’s disparate factions weigh possible governing arrangements, including a unity government bringing rival factions together or a minority government reliant on outside support. If they fail to reach an agreement, Israel could head back to the polls.
Here’s what you should know:
The pro-Netanyahu coalition won 53 seats:
A bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats:
Arab-led parties won 19 seats:
That leaves all existing blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, meaning some parties would have to realign or join forces across bloc lines to form a new government.
Israel’s election results must be officially certified and presented to President Isaac Herzog by November 4 .
The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10 .
Herzog must task one incoming Knesset member with forming a new government by November 11 . He is expected to make his decision with input from party leaders, selecting the candidate he believes has the best chance of building a coalition.
The candidate commissioned by Herzog has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible extension of 14 days .
He has not said yet, but the most likely candidates are Netanyahu or former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party received the most votes in the opposition bloc.
According to Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth media, Eisenkot may have an edge over Netanyahu as some Arab-led parties consider endorsing him in a bid to oust Netanyahu.
Herzog, for his part, has urged Israeli politicians to move away from rigid partisan stances and look for “creative solutions” that will lead to a new government and avoid a second round of elections.
Before the election, Herzog said he would do everything he could to spare the country another election cycle, even if that means pressing for a national unity government that brings together rivals Netanyahu and Eisenkot.
Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have previously ruled out partnering with the Arab-led parties .
Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, however, has said he believes they “can change their mind”, arguing that Netanyahu would do in their position.
“If Netanyahu had a similar problem, he would immediately invite Mansour Abbas”, the leader of Ra’am and “give him the role of a minister of interior”, Barak told France 24 on Friday.
Abbas himself has signalled a willingness to work the opposition camp, saying Eisenkot’s conditions would not pose an obstacle for his party, according to Israel’s Channel 12.
Yousef Jabareen from the Arab-led Joint List has also said that his party is ready for the “ousting of the Netanyahu government”.
“The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership,” he wrote on X.
Even if Arab-led parties do not formally join the opposition’s coalition, they could prop it up from outside by helping it pass a confidence vote in the Knesset.
Raluca Ganea, co-founder of Israeli civil society group Zazim, told Al Jazeera that a coalition between the opposition bloc and the Arab-led parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel “is the only path forward for Israeli democracy as a whole”.
If Herzog’s first candidate fails to form a government within the 42 days, the Israeli president has the option of asking another Knesset member to try to do so within 28 days. If that candidate also fails, a majority of Knesset members could put forward a third candidate, who would have a final 14 days to try to assemble one.
Even without a coalition commanding at least 61 seats, a candidate could still try to form a minority government by relying on outside support from smaller parties, including Arab-led parties, or negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with alternating prime ministers.
If none of these options succeed and deadlock persists, the Knesset would be formally dissolved, and Israelis would return to the polls for another round of elections.
Those elections would have to be called within 90 days.
Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.
If the process drags out, that could leave Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in power for months more, even if he ultimately fails to become part of the next governing coalition.
